newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Congress seen passing 97 budget in Nov..
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Congress seen passing 97 budget in Nov..

text.p: A political agreement between opposition and government parties opened the way for legislative approval of the Venezuelan government's 7.8 trillion-bolivar ($16.6 billion) 1997 budget before the end of congressional sessions next week, legislators said Thursday.
"We will definitely approve the budget next week because we are working on it flat out," said Juan Sosa Mauri of the government Convergence party.
The political agreement was reached after the government reallocated about 355 billion bolivars ($755 million) from government debt payments to a decentralization fund and other areas like education.

Opposition parties had clashed with the government over the amount set aside for transferring responsibilities and functions to regional governments. Other reallocations were made to boost spending on education, science and technology and water supply which were also deemed to be insufficient.

Debt payments now left out of the budget will be met from additional spending requests made during the course of the year, Sosa Mauri said. It was not clear if the debt payments are due to foreign or domestic creditors or a combination of both.
The Chamber of Deputies Finance Committee is working on a report to recommend approval of the budget in chamber on Tuesday, he said.

Final approval by the Senate could come on Wednesday if the discussion is considered under a legislative motion called constitutional urgency, which allows legislation to be passed in one vote instead of the customary two.
Rodrigo Cabezas, deputy with opposition party Radical Cause said, however, that "it is most likely that it will be approved on Thursday."
The budget proposal must be approved by the end of Congressional ordinary sessions on Nov 30 to prevent a roll-over budget based on revenues and spending in 1996.
